newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia indicts Soros foundation for tax evasion.
newsitem.headline: Croatia indicts Soros foundation for tax evasion.

text.p: Croatia on Thursday indicted three senior officials from a local branch of an international humanitarian foundation sponsored by U.S. billionaire George Soros for alleged financial malpractice and tax evasion.

The indictment came after weeks of anti-Soros campaigning initiated by President Franjo Tudjman at the annual congress of his nationalist ruling HDZ party in November, where he branded Soros as enemy of the state.

Croatian police stormed the premises of the Soros-sponsored "Open Society" in Zagreb two weeks ago and said it found evidence of "illegal financial transactions" that the Society had allegedly been performing for the last twelve months.

According to the state news agency HINA the Zagreb public prosecutor on Thursday pressed charges against Open Society's director Karmen Basic, executive director Srdjan Dvornik and accountant Ivanka Marton.

The prosecutor charged that Soros employees had been receiving double salaries since December last year -- a regular one in Croatian currency (kuna) and another in U.S. dollars, which was not reported for state tax.
The unpaid taxes total 2.7 million kuna ($490,000)," the indictment said.
It was not clear what penalties the three might face.

In his November address Tudjman said the U.S.-based foundation had "infiltrated" the entire Croatian society, particularly cultural institutions and the media with the aim of changing their ownership structure.
He accused Soros and "other American and European foundations" of supporting his opponents, helping small magazines and systematically enlarging their activities.
Shortly after that police confiscated $65,000 from two Soros foundation members at a border crossing. The two were released after interrogation but the money was not returned.
